winner_reason: SpaceX acquiring xAI to build space-based AI data centers is a highly novel, high-impact infrastructure story with strong long-tail SEO potential around power, cooling, and regulation of off-planet compute. Even after a diversity penalty for repeating the Data/Infra bucket, it clearly out-scores the other events.

scored.notes: Major corporate move combining two Musk entities with a concrete, controversial vision: shifting AI compute into space. Impact: high novelty, large audiences (SpaceX/xAI/Musk), strong regulatory and geopolitical angles. SEO: strong for explainers on space-based data centers, AI energy use, orbital infra, jurisdiction; good evergreen value as a reference piece. Diversity: Data/Infra appears twice in the last 6 posts, so max 6-point penalty (no override, as news_impact < 22 threshold for special treatment).

Ethics/analysis piece on AI as a layoff justification. Impact: important but more interpretive than event-driven; limited to labor/employment/HR audiences. SEO: solid for terms like 'AI layoffs', 'AI-washing', but partially tied to current cycle; some evergreen angle around governance and disclosure standards. No recent Ethics bucket, so no diversity penalty.

Apple–Google Gemini integration in Siri is a major platform shift with big user reach and competition/privacy implications. Impact: very high in consumer ecosystem terms, but still pre-announcement and based on reporting rather than a launched product. SEO: excellent for queries on 'Gemini Siri', 'Apple Google AI deal', on-device vs cloud assistants; strong explainer potential. Models bucket has been used 3 times in the last 6 posts, so full 6-point penalty. News impact stays below override threshold, so penalty stands.

Nvidia pitching an Android-for-robots stack at CES is important for robotics ecosystems and chip/platform lock-in. Impact: solid but more directional/roadmap than disruptive event; limited beyond robotics/industrial readers. SEO: good for 'generalist robotics', 'Nvidia robot foundation models'; some ongoing value. Robotics appears twice in last 6 posts, plus twice in last 4, so 6-point penalty.

Startup profile of Physical Intelligence. Impact: interesting signal about generalist robot 'brains' but narrower audience; more VC/startup interest than broad news. SEO: decent for 'robot brain startup', 'generalist robot control models', but less evergreen and more company-specific. Same Robotics bucket and same penalty reasoning as index 3.

Carbon Robotics’ crop-vs-weed model is a concrete, applied edge AI story in agriculture. Impact: strong for ag-tech and automation but not a global platform shift; more sectoral. SEO: good around 'AI weeding', 'laser weeder', 'edge AI agriculture', with case-study style evergreen value. Edge AI bucket appears once in last 6 but not in the last 4 and not consecutively, so no penalty.

General analysis of workforce shifts from AI in creative and knowledge work. Impact: thematic and diffuse, no single anchor event; important but less newsy. SEO: decent for 'AI and creative jobs', 'AI impact on knowledge workers', but highly competitive space and somewhat generic. No recent Creative AI bucket, so no penalty.

Talent consolidation around big labs like OpenAI. Impact: meaningful for industry structure and competition, but gradual trend rather than a single inflection point. SEO: moderate; fits into 'AI talent war', 'OpenAI hiring' narratives, but many similar pieces exist. Models bucket is already heavily used, so full 6-point penalty applies.
